title: 2 Enoch

translation.name: 2 Enoch — N. Forbes and R. H. Charles (1913)
translation.translator: N. Forbes and R. H. Charles
translation.edition: 2 Enoch, or The Book of the Secrets of Enoch, translated from the Slavonic, in R. H. Charles (ed.), The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, vol. 2 (Oxford, 1913); reprinted in R. H. Platt (ed.), The Forgotten Books of Eden (1926)

rightsNote: N. Forbes (1883–1929) and R. H. Charles (d. 1931), published 1913. Public domain in the United States, and in the United Kingdom and the EU since 2002.
editorialMarkers: Survives only in Slavonic, in a longer and a shorter recension; this is the longer, as Forbes and Charles printed it. Wikisource’s page credits R. H. Platt as translator, which he was not — he edited the 1926 volume that reprints the 1913 translation, and the translators are named above. Not part of the Ethiopian canon: 1 Enoch is, 2 Enoch is not.
citation: Forbes, N., and R. H. Charles. “2 Enoch, or the Book of the Secrets of Enoch.” In The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, ed. R. H. Charles, vol. 2. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1913. Public domain. Wikisource transcription of the 1926 reprint.
